title: NHS gender dysphoria clinics
description: You and your GP may agree that you should see specialists at a gender dysphoria clinic so you can consider your treatment options. Here's how to find one.
body:
If you think you have gender dysphoria or incongruence , your particular needs may be best addressed by health services offered by NHS gender dysphoria clinics (GDCs). A GP or another healthcare professional can refer you directly to one of the GDCs. The websites of the clinics listed on this page also have useful information for you to think about before you see a GP.

Children and young people's gender services

Children and young people can be referred to the National Referral Support Service for the NHS Children and Young People's Gender Service . These NHS services specialise in helping young people aged 17 and under with symptoms of gender dysphoria or incongruence. They take referrals from anywhere in England.

Tavistock Centre 120 Belize Lane London NW3 5BA Phone: 020 8938 7590 Email: gic@tavi-port.nhs.uk The gender identity clinic (GIC) website has useful information for anyone with gender identity needs, not just those in the area.

TransPlus

56 Dean Street SOHO London W1D 6AQ Phone: 020 3315 9576 Email: chelwest.transplusinfo@nhs.net The TransPlus website has information about the services and support it offers.

NHS gender dysphoria pilot services

The NHS is running pilot gender clinics for adults across the country. A pilot service is a new NHS service that is tested with a small number of people to see if it works well before it's offered more widely. These services are delivered by healthcare professionals with specialist skills and are based in community and sexual health services. NHS England is assessing how useful these pilot services are.
